note: The bands the Wot 4 plant has to land in, from docs/WOT4-STAGE1.md, which derives each from Chris Foss's published figures for the Wot 4 (590 sq in, 70 to 90 oz, his electric conversion), the Ripmax Wot 4 Mk2 ARTF's manual (span, balance, throws), AXI's figures for the 4120/14 and RCM&E's reviews (scripts/wot4-derive.js prints the derived figures). Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

w1_level_75.source: level at three quarter throttle, the trim, derived 17.35; the band 15 percent either side, the elevator near neutral

w2_stall.source: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax), derived 9.32; alphaStall is CLmax / CLalpha, 1.098 / 4.752; the band the Edge's in proportion, 6 percent under and 14 over

w3_glide.source: L/D at 1.4 Vs, 13.05 m/s, derived 8.31; 11 percent either side

w4_top.source: level at full throttle, derived 23.59; the Edge's band in proportion, 9 percent under and 10 over

w5_roll.source: full aileron at the manual's 9 mm from level at 20 m/s: the helix angle over the first half second derived 0.1028 through the surface's knee (177 deg/s), 20 percent either side. Crisp: 90 percent of that rate within a quarter second (the roll mode's time constant is derived 0.04 s). Axial: the ailerons' adverse yaw, rudder centred, swings the nose off the path by the sideslip the linear lateral model derives over that first half second, 7.7 deg, 35 percent under and 50 over: no source gives a Wot 4's, so the band holds the plant to its derivation and the pilot's touch of rudder is what makes the roll axial (a whole roll takes over 2 s, and gravity bends the path through it: recorded, not banded)

w5_low.source: the low end of the manual's ranges, 6 mm of aileron and 9 of elevator: derived 0.0713, 20 percent either side

w7_vertical.source: full throttle straight up, T(V) = W + q S CD0, derived 9.24, 10 percent either side; Foss: the conversion 'will hold a vertical climb from take-off on a freshly charged battery'

w8_inverted.source: RCM&E's review of the Wot 4 (Ashby, 2006): 'my example needed only a breath of down elevator to hold inverted flight'. The figure: at full throttle, the stick on its back less the stick upright, on the linear model through the knee and the expo, derived 0.297; 25 percent either side; the speed within 10 percent of upright

w9_loop.source: big loops: from level at full throttle, half up stick held, the loop spans 30 m or more and goes over the top at 1.3 Vs or more without the wing stalling anywhere. The derivation's loop pulled at CL 0.6 spans 45 m and goes over the top at 16.4 m/s, 1.76 Vs; the criterion is this document's

w10_stall.source: the docile stall: from 14 m/s, the throttle closed, the stick eased to full back over 4 s and held 6: past the stall, the wings stay within 10 deg of level and it does not turn. RCM&E on the WOT4e (Tuszynski, 2012): 'The stall was a non-event. The aircraft slowed to the point that it was just gently descending vertically in a high alpha position, wings remaining level'; Foss: 'docile and forgiving'. A trainer drops a wing under 30 deg (docs/STALL-STAGE1.md): a third of that

w11_spin.source: RCM&E (Ashby, 2006): 'The model spins and flicks with ease and recovers well'. Full up and full rudder, power off, from 14 m/s, held 4 s: past the stall it turns the rudder's way, a quarter turn at least ('in the direction of rudder application', FAA-H-8083-3C ch. 5); then hands off, every stick centred, the rotation under 30 deg/s with the wing unstalled within 0.5 s and a quarter turn. The plant turns it as a steep spiral at about 45 deg/s, not a flat spin: docs/WOT4-STAGE1.md, what is open

w12_knife.source: a knife edge pass at full throttle, rolled to 90 deg in a second and full rudder held for 2 s more: the fuselage and fin's side force and the thrust carry 39 percent of the weight at the rudder's 18 deg of sideslip, the wash over the rudder and the fin included, derived at 21 m/s, the rest sinking it at 5.95 m/s^2 (the sink speed's growth over the pass); 35 percent either side. A pass, not a sustained knife edge: it cannot hold its height on its side. The coupling: the high wing and the rudder over the CG roll it, which the pilot holds with 0.122 of full aileron, derived; half again either side

w6_prop_torque.source: static full throttle, rolling left: ideal disc power 439 W at 8,303 rpm, 0.505 N m; the Edge's band in proportion

w13_rest.source: the drawn model at rest, derived 12.53 deg and 0.2121 m, 13.3 percent on the tail; 1 deg, 6 mm and 3 to 4 points of the tail's share either side

w14_takeoff.source: the throttle opened over a second and a half on grass, the tail up at 6 m/s, rotated at 1.2 Vs: derived liftoff 7.45 m at 11.82 m/s; the Edge's bands, 27 percent under and 45 over, and 15 percent either side

w14_straight.source: the same take off with the pilot's feet on the rudder and the tailwheel it steers: it tracks

w15_taxi.source: full right rudder at walking pace, 0.28 throttle, 2.7 N of thrust against 1.8 N of rolling resistance once it moves: the wire tailwheel epoxied in the rudder steers at its angle, the wheelbase over tan of 30.4 deg, derived 1.46 m, 25 percent either side, turning right

w16_landing.source: easy landings: a power off approach at 1.3 Vs, a round out and hold off no higher than the three point attitude, and the tail held down: it touches at 1.3 Vs (12.1 m/s) or slower, does not bounce, and rolls to rest at W13's attitude with no hull or prop contact. RCM&E's WOT4e: 'landing at walking pace'

w17_unmoved.source: the five inch's canonical replay hash and every other aircraft's recorded flight hash in Node, from main's module at 3637fef, before the Wot 4 existed, and the Zagi's and the Ugly Stik's from main's at 4223337, when they had merged: its table moves none of them

w18_cross_host.source: the Wot 4's recorded take off, roll, loop, stall and spin, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome
